quotes.text: Your eyes deserve a moment of rest.
Take care of the eyes through which you experience life.
Let your eyes wander somewhere far away for a moment.
Soft focus, slow breath, gentle eyes.
Your eyes have been working hard. Give them a short holiday.
Look up, look out, look far.
Blink slowly. Let your eyes feel the pause.
The screen will still be here. Let your eyes travel somewhere else.
Find the farthest thing you can see and rest your gaze there.
Give your eyes a view that is not made of pixels.
Close your eyes for a moment and notice how good it feels.
Distance is a gift to tired eyes.
Let the horizon do the work for a while.
Comfortable eyes make for a calmer mind.
Every glance away from the screen is a small kindness.
Your eyes are not machines. Treat them gently.
Relax your gaze. Nothing needs your focus right now.
Let the details blur for a moment. That is the point.
Your work can wait. Your health cannot.
A small pause today builds healthier habits tomorrow.
Look away from the screen and reconnect with the world.
Thirty seconds of stillness can reset an entire hour.
Pausing is not quitting. It is pacing.
Short breaks, often, beat long breaks, rarely.
This pause is part of the work, not a break from it.
Step back so you can see clearly again.
A break taken now is better than a break needed later.
The best time for a break is before you feel you need one.
Let this moment be unhurried.
Breathe in. Breathe out. That counts as progress.
Stand up, stretch, and come back fresh.
Nothing important will be lost in the next minute.
Give yourself permission to pause.
Every break is a small reset button.
You have earned this pause.
Healthy habits are built one small pause at a time.
Consistency beats intensity, especially for rest.
Good habits are quiet. They just keep showing up.
The habit of resting is as valuable as the habit of working.
Small routines, repeated daily, shape how you feel.
Twenty minutes, twenty feet, twenty seconds. Easy to remember, easy to do.
A reminder is only useful if you listen to it. Thank you for listening.
Build a rhythm your body can keep up with.
Today's small choices become tomorrow's routines.
Make rest automatic, not occasional.
You do not need willpower for this. You just need to pause.
Taking breaks is a skill. You are practising it right now.
Healthy screen habits start with moments like this.
Habits are easier to keep than to rebuild. Keep this one.
Rest is part of doing good work.
Rest is not a reward. It is a requirement.
A rested mind solves problems a tired one cannot see.
Stillness is productive too.
Recovery is where the effort pays off.
You are allowed to slow down.
Quiet moments refill what busy hours drain.
Rest well now so you can focus well later.
Let your shoulders drop and your jaw relax.
Doing nothing for a moment is doing something for yourself.
Even machines need to cool down.
Pause long enough to notice how you feel.
Calm is a resource. Take a little now.
There is strength in stepping back.
Productivity is not measured by how long you ignore your health.
You are more than your to-do list.
Work is important. So are you.
The world beyond the screen is still there. Go say hello.
Balance is not found. It is made, one pause at a time.
Take care of yourself the way you take care of your work.
Your best work comes from a well-cared-for you.
Look out the window. Life is happening there too.
Unplug for a moment and plug back into yourself.
Deadlines come and go. Your well-being stays with you.
Make room for the things that keep you well.
A sustainable pace is the fastest pace over time.
Some things matter more than the next email.
Be as generous with your rest as you are with your effort.
Sustainable productivity starts with a sustainable you.
Focus is renewable. Breaks are how you renew it.
Fresh eyes catch what tired eyes miss.
Working longer is not the same as working better.
A clear head is the best productivity tool you own.
Great work is a marathon, not a sprint.
Short pauses keep long days manageable.
The quality of your attention matters more than the quantity of your hours.
Come back to your work with a new perspective.
Smart work includes smart rest.
Momentum survives a short break. Fatigue does not go away without one.
Recharge now; you will thank yourself this afternoon.
Progress loves a rested mind.
Better focus comes after a moment of letting go.
Your body has been sitting still. Give it a reason to move.
Roll your shoulders back and take a deep breath.
Notice your posture. Then gently improve it.
Have a sip of water while you are here.
Unclench your jaw. Relax your hands.
A few deep breaths can change the tone of your whole day.
Kindness to yourself counts as self-care.
Feel your feet on the floor for a moment.
Stretch your arms up high and let them fall slowly.
Your well-being is worth a minute of your time.
Move a little. Your body will appreciate it.
Check in with yourself: how are you feeling right now?
Breathe slowly enough to notice it.
Look after your body; it carries all of your work.
Small acts of care add up over a lifetime.

instructions: Look at something about 20 feet (6 metres) away and relax your eyes.
Blink slowly and naturally a few times.
Close your eyes gently and take three slow breaths.
Look out of a window and let your eyes rest on the far distance.
Relax your shoulders and let your hands rest in your lap.
Stand up and stretch your arms above your head.
Step away from the screen for a moment.
Slowly look up, down, left and right, then rest your gaze far away.
Roll your shoulders backwards a few times.
Unclench your jaw and soften the muscles around your eyes.
Gently turn your head from side to side.
